item.title: Unearthing Duke Forest Celebration & Tour — Sat Nov 21, 9:00 AM — None
item.description:
Join us on Saturday, November 21, from 9:00-11:00 a.m. for the official launch of the new Unearthing Duke Forest Trail near the Wooden Bridge in the Korstian Division.
Through three newly installed signs, visitors can explore some of the rich and complex human history of the land that is today called the Duke Forest and learn about historic features that remain visible on the land today.
The event will feature remarks from project leaders and contributors, a guided opportunity to experience the trail, and time to celebrate the many individuals and partners who helped bring this project to life.
This event is part of the We the People initiative, a Duke and Durham collaboration commemorating the 250th anniversary of the United States through public programs that explore our shared history, evolving identity, and collective future.
Source: Duke Arts, Duke University

item.title: A World of Weird and Wonderful Plants: Duke Research Greenhouse Tour — Sat Nov 21, 10:00 AM — Duke Research Greenhouse–Directions to Follow
item.description: Join Alec Motten, professor emeritus, Duke University Department of Biology, on a guided tour of the Duke Research Greenhouse’s teaching collection, which includes amazing specimens from a wide diversity of terrestrial habitats, ranging from hot, dry deserts to humid tropical rainforests. Marvel at the diverse ways plants have evolved to live in very different habitats, and compare the striking modifications in color, shape and anatomical features that allow them to thrive and survive in extreme environments. Also admire the teaching collection’s impressive array of carnivorous plants from all over the world—not only North Carolina and North America, but also South America, Australia and Southeast Asia. Closely examine the myriad ingenious ways carnivorous plants have evolved to capture and consume their animal prey. Location: Duke Research Greenhouse; directions will be included in program reminder email sent the week before. Fee: $30, 20% discount for Duke Gardens members with disc

item.description: 5 Points Gallery, an artist-owned contemporary art gallery in downtown Durham, is pleased to announce an exhibition of paintings by Featured Artist King Nobuyoshi Godwin, whose vibrant, imaginative work reflects his experience of autism and synesthesia. Bringing together expressive animals, vivid colors, and numbers that convey emotion, Godwin creates playful worlds filled with unexpected connections. In a painting inspired by the African shoebill, King transforms the imposing bird into a potential friend, welcoming it into his colorful world of unlikely companions. Throughout the gallery, visitors can also enjoy work by our Triangle-based artists, offering a refreshing mix of painting, sculpture, fused glass, mixed media, and finely crafted furniture, with each artist bringing a distinct creative perspective. What emerges is HEYZ’s pursuit of originality over comfort. item.title: Calichi Trio Concert — Sun Nov 22, 3:00 PM — East Duke 201 - Nelson Music Room
item.description:
Experience the artistry and expressive range of the Calichi Trio, featuring Duke Music faculty members Ieva Jokubaviciute, piano; Hsiao-Mei Ku, violin; and Caroline Stinson, cello.
The program pairs Johann Nepomuk Hummel's graceful and spirited Piano Trio in E-flat Major, Op. 12, with Dmitri Shostakovich's powerful Piano Trio No. 2 in E Minor, Op. 67. Spanning contrasting musical worlds, these works move from Classical elegance and sparkling interplay to profound intensity, emotional depth, and dramatic urgency.
Together, the three musicians bring this compelling repertoire to life through intimate musical conversation, remarkable ensemble playing, and the rich combination of piano, violin, and cello.
This event is free and open to the public. All are welcome.

item.title: CEE Seminar - Intelligent Structures: Harnessing Physical Dynamics as a Computational Resource — Mon Nov 23, 12:00 PM — None
item.description: In living systems, the morphology of the body is tightly coupled to the robustness and speed of the sense-assess-respond feedback loop for optimal flight control, maneuverability and many other functions. The concept of "embodiment" emphasizes the significant role that physical shape, mechanical compliance, and multi-functionality can play in facilitating feedback responses that point toward intelligent behavior and control. Using the mathematical framework of reservoir computing, it is possible to harness these intrinsic mechanical behaviors and dynamics from the loading environment as a computational resource. In this presentation, we will evaluate the information processing capacity of several physical reservoir computing systems, including a fluid structure interaction model, a magnetomechanical resonator, and an optomechanical spring network. item.description:

Please join AGS for an Evening with Brett McGurk on Monday, November 23rd.
Brett McGurk is a diplomat, presidential advisor, CNN Global Affairs Analyst, and author. He has served in four presidential administrations across both parties and has been deeply involved in Middle East military strategy, diplomacy, and U.S. policy for more than two decades. He has served directly for the last four presidents, negotiated multiple hostage releases, built the international coalition that ultimately defeated ISIS, and engaged regularly and directly with leaders from across the Middle East and around the world.
Mr. McGurk offers insight into complex world problems, and how he built successful coalitions, advised four very different presidents, and acted as a steady and reliable leader to resolve seemingly insurmountable conflicts-earning strong bipartisan support in our divisive times. item.title: Kudzu and Wisteria Basket Weaving — Sun Nov 29, 10:00 AM — Duke Gardens–Pelham-Cullen Classroom in the Barnes Welcome Center
item.description: Learn to weave a basket with kudzu and wisteria, invasive species that grow quickly and plentifully throughout the Southeast, with instructor Angela Eastman of Flag Mountain Studio. The mature vines of both plants can be harvested and processed into bark strips and woody material that form the structure for strong and beautiful baskets. In learning traditional wicker weaving techniques to work with this plentiful material, you’ll connect to a long human lineage of working with natural materials to create useful vessels. You can expect to leave with a small basket or platter woven from kudzu and wisteria. Throughout the day together, as you build creative community and ecological awareness, Angela will invite a new way to understand “weeds” in the environment where they live, shifting perspectives to view these plants as creative collaborators and resourceful cohabiters. The invitation is simply to slow down, work with the natural materials and create something that feels meaningful to you. Individual panels will be brought together in a large, quilt-like installation, transforming many distinct creations into a shared work of art.
